title: 2008 AMC 10A Problem 16
statement: Points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on a circle centered at \(O,\) and \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ.\) A second circle is internally tangent to the first and tangent to both \(OA\) and \(OB.\) What is the ratio of the area of the smaller circle to that of the larger circle?

solutions.text:
Let the radii be \(r\) and \(R.\) The small circle’s center \(E\) lies on the bisector of \(\angle AOB,\) so \(OE\) makes a \(30^\circ\) angle with \(OA.\)

The perpendicular from \(E\) to \(OA\) has length \(r,\) and in the resulting \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle \(OE = 2r.\)

Since \(OE = R - r,\) we get \(2r = R - r,\) so \(R = 3r\) and the area ratio is \(\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{9}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The small circle’s center lies on the bisector of \(\angle AOB\)
The center is \(2r\) from \(O\) by a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle, and also \(R - r\) from \(O\)
